visual_failures: R2 makes the effects visible, but the muzzle is two oversized blurred neon-yellow cones/discs. It reads as a debug particle test rather than a compact industrial shotgun flash.
The muzzle has no controlled white-hot core, thin pressure ring, hot-brass hierarchy or sharp directional micro-streak design. Its scale competes with and would obscure the approved body.
The impact contact and decay are bundles of thick fluorescent yellow rods. They do not read as contact core, kinetic fan, rivet sparks, pressure ring or residue cloud.

All VFX roles collapse to one yellow value and one soft cylindrical/beam shape. There is no material, timing, scale or shape hierarchy comparable to the Gunner_Bullet/Fighter_Attack baseline or the user's school example.

Flight improves only by exposing static white needles and brown pellets. The attached particle wake remains visually absent and the lines are too uniform and disconnected from the drum's rear load path.
The body lighting is improved and remains acceptable for this QA pass, but visible body transport cannot compensate for failed Muzzle, Flight and Impact art direction.

derived_vfx_rebuild_contract.scope: New StrictCustomDerived prefabs and materials only. Approved body FBX, external body materials, body hierarchy and original source prefabs remain read-only.
muzzle: Author a compact one-shot industrial rivet flash around +Z: one white-hot contact core, one short warm-brass wedge, one thin expanding pressure ring and 6-10 unequal sharp micro-streaks.
Keep the visible envelope roughly body-mouth scale, not multiple body diameters. No paired bulbous cones, giant discs, uniform yellow fog or helper lights.
Use separate HDR value roles: pale machining-white core, warm brass/orange accent and a low-alpha cool gray pressure/smoke component.
flight: Keep the approved drum and asymmetric pellet anchors. Re-seat the seven static streaks to the rear load direction and vary length/offset so they do not form parallel floating needles.
Author an attached compact wake no longer than about one-third to one-half body length: 3-5 clean pale streaks, a restrained uneven hot-brass pellet flicker and sparse dark scrap dust.
At gameplay scale the body remains primary, but the wake must be visible without a macro camera.
impact: Author a compact white-hot contact core, one thin directional pressure ring/fan, 7-12 unequal tapered hot-brass and pale rivet sparks, and one short low-alpha dark oxide/brass residue cloud.
Contact must read as a single forceful strike rather than crossed rods. Decay must retain a soft residue mass for a short interval before fully cleaning.
Avoid thick glowing cylinders, neon-lime/yellow uniformity, symmetric starbursts, screen-filling bloom and unrelated meshes.
technical: You may replace ParticleSystem module values and render settings inside the derived M/F/I prefabs because R2 proved exact legacy serialization is not a viable commercial result. Do not modify source prefabs.
Use Unity 6 compatible URP Particles/Unlit or verified project particle shaders with explicit additive/alpha blend, correct HDR colors, textures and renderer alignment.
Retain +Z forward semantics, deterministic fixed-rig timing and the standalone M/F/I nesting with no runtime/controller/catalog/MFI components.
Recapture at least M peak, F hero/macro/gameplay, I contact/decay, M/F/I cleanup and the two baselines comparison. Run all three 30-cycle cleanup tests and report new Console errors as zero.

root_note: R2 solves invisibility but exposes the underlying problem: the legacy-derived systems do not form a commercial effect. Rebuild only the new derived VFX with a compact white-hot/brass/dark-oxide hierarchy, keep the approved body untouched, and prove it again in the fixed rig.
